mainTopic: The בכור's double portion: owning it before division, whether a father can cancel it, how to prove who is the בכור, and the טומטום
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of a בכור who sold his extra share before the brothers divided the estate. Two Sages explain the ruling 'he did nothing' in different ways. A ruling from ארץ ישראל suggests the בכור owns nothing before division, but the גמרא rules that he does, and the story of מר זוטרא and רב אשי shows this in practice. Next, a new משנה teaches that a father cannot cancel a son's Torah inheritance or a בכור's double portion. He can still divide his property unequally if he gives it as a מתנה. The גמרא shows that this fits even רבי יהודה, because the son never agreed to give up his rights. רב יוסף then teaches which words of a father prove a son is his בכור, and two stories test that rule. Finally, רבי אמי and רב נחמן בר יצחק teach that a טומטום later found to be male is neither a בכור nor a בן סורר ומורה, because he must be a known son from birth.

steps.title: Two ways to understand 'he did nothing'
steps.stepSummary: Two Sages explain רבא's ruling about a בכור who sold before division. One says the sale fails only for half. The other says it fails for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: 'he did nothing' means only for half (his brother's share). The other Sage holds: it means for all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining what רבא meant when he said a בכור who sold before the division 'did nothing.' There are two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first view (רב פפי), the sale fails only for the part that is really his brother's, because the בכור already owns his own extra share. According to the second view (רב פפא), the whole sale fails, because the בכור does not own his extra share at all until the estate is divided. So the real question is whether the extra share belongs to the בכור before division.

keyTerms.meaning: He has done nothing (the act has no effect)
All of them / all of it

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets up the key question for the rest of the section: does a בכור own his double portion before the estate is divided?

phrases.english: One Sage holds: he has done nothing
with regard to half.
phrases.notes: He means the half that belongs to his brother. His own extra share was sold properly.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds: with regard to all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבא's ruling about a בכור who sold before division.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: the sale fails only for the brother's half. Other view: the sale fails entirely.

steps.title: A ruling sent from ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל rule that a בכור who sold before division did nothing. The גמרא concludes from this that they hold he has no right to his extra share before division.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from ארץ ישראל: A בכור who sold before the division did nothing. This shows that, in their view, the בכור has no extra share before the division.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from the scholars of ארץ ישראל. It then explains the principle behind that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling says the sale has no effect at all. The word אלמא (apparently) draws the reason: the sale must fail because the בכור does not own his extra share yet. This matches the second view in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there (from ארץ ישראל)
Firstborn son, who inherits a double portion

phrases.english: They sent from there:
A firstborn who sold before the division
has done nothing.
Apparently, the firstborn does not have [his extra share]
before the division.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside ruling that supports the view that the whole sale fails.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale by a בכור before division has no effect, because he has no extra share before division.

steps.title: The final ruling: the בכור does own his share before division
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules against the view from ארץ ישראל. The בכור does have his extra share even before division.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is: the בכור has his extra share before the division.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה, and it goes against the ruling just quoted from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the extra share is already his, a בכור who sells it before division has made a valid sale of his own part. This fits the first view in step 1, which said the sale fails only for the brother's half.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is (the final practical ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: יש לבכור קודם חלוקה. The בכור already owns his double portion before the estate is divided.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the ruling from ארץ ישראל. The גמרא brings it and then rules against it.

phrases.english: But the halacha is: the firstborn has [his extra share]
before the division.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the principle drawn from the ruling of ארץ ישראל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A בכור owns his extra portion even before the estate is divided.

steps.title: מר זוטרא splits the peppers equally
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, a בכור, split a basket of peppers equally with his brothers. Later he asked for a double portion of the rest. רב אשי ruled that he had given up his extra share in everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא of the house of רישבא split a basket of peppers equally with his brothers. He came before רב אשי. רב אשי told him: Since you gave up your extra share in part of the estate, you gave it up in all of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the הלכה from step 3 in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra share already belonged to מר זוטרא before division. So when he chose to split the peppers equally, he was giving up something that was really his. רב אשי treats that as giving up his extra share in the whole estate, not just in the peppers.
steps.whatToRemember: A בכור who gives up his double portion in even part of the estate has given it up in all of it.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra of the house of Rishba
divided a basket of peppers
with the brothers, equally.
He came before Rav Ashi,
he said to him: Since you gave up on part,
you have given up on all of the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא מִדְּרִישְׁבָּא פְּלַג בְּצַנָּא דְפִלְפְּלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the הלכה that יש לבכור קודם חלוקה in an actual case.
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה that a בכור owns his extra share before division
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's ruling in the case of מר זוטרא

steps.title: A father cannot cancel his son's Torah inheritance
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a father says his בכור will not get a double portion, or that a son will not inherit with his brothers, his words have no effect. He is making a condition against the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who says 'My son so-and-so, the בכור, will not take a double portion,' or 'My son so-and-so will not inherit with his brothers' has said nothing. This is because he made a condition against what is written in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a father cannot change the Torah's inheritance rules just by saying so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double portion of the בכור and the equal inheritance of sons are set by the Torah. A plain statement that tries to cancel them is a condition against the Torah, so it has no legal power.

keyTerms.meaning: He has said nothing (his words have no effect)
He made a condition against what is written in the Torah

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who says:
"So-and-so, my firstborn son,
will not take a double portion";
or "So-and-so, my son,
will not inherit with his brothers"
has said nothing,
since he made a condition against what is written in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי בְּנִי בְּכוֹר לֹא יִטּוֹל פִּי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: whether a father can change the Torah's inheritance rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's statement that cancels a son's Torah inheritance or a בכור's double portion has no effect.

steps.title: Dividing property as a gift works, but not as inheritance
steps.stepSummary: A father who gives out his property by speaking may give unequal shares, or make the בכור equal to his brothers, and his words stand. If he says it is ירושה, his words mean nothing. If he writes the word מתנה anywhere in the document, his words stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man divides his property by word of mouth, giving more to one son and less to another, or making the firstborn equal to the others, his words stand. But if he said he was giving it as inheritance, he has said nothing. If he wrote that it is a gift, whether at the beginning, the middle, or the end, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from Step 5. It shows the right way a father can change how his sons share his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, the father failed because he tried to change the Torah's inheritance rules. Here he reaches nearly the same result by calling it a מתנה (gift), and a gift is fully in his control. The label matters: 'ירושה' fails, 'מתנה' works, and the gift wording can appear anywhere in the document.

keyTerms.meaning: One who divides up his property

steps.whatToRemember: A father cannot rewrite the Torah's inheritance rules. He can still give his property away as a gift however he wants.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict Step 5. The outcome can be similar, but a gift and an inheritance are different legal routes. Only the gift route is in the father's hands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical way a person can divide his estate unequally without going against the Torah's laws of ירושה.

phrases.english: One who divides his property by his mouth (orally);
he gave more to one and less to another,
or made the firstborn equal to them,
his words stand.
But if he said it is as inheritance,
he has said nothing.
If he wrote, whether at the beginning,
phrases.notes: He means the word 'gift' appears somewhere in the document. Where it appears does not matter.

phrases.english: or in the middle, or at the end,
that it is as a gift, his words stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in Step 5 by showing the valid path, a gift, after Step 5 rejected the invalid path, changing inheritance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unequal division of property works if it is given as מתנה. It fails if it is called ירושה.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה (Step 5) does not follow רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה holds that in money matters, a condition against the Torah does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let us say our משנה is not like רבי יהודה. For if it were רבי יהודה, doesn't he say that in a money matter, his condition stands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a suggestion. Maybe the משנה's rule that a father cannot cancel the בכור's double share goes against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the father's condition fails because it goes against the Torah. Inheritance is about money. If רבי יהודה allows conditions against the Torah in money matters, then by his view the father's condition should work. So the משנה seems to follow only the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (the גמרא testing a suggestion)
Not in line with רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Gemara:
Let us say that our Mishnah
is not in line with Rabbi Yehuda?
For if it were Rabbi Yehuda,
doesn't he say:
in a money matter, his condition stands!
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 5, where the father's condition failed because it went against the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and tests whose view the משנה's ruling in Step 5 follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling (Step 5) that a father's condition against the בכור's double share has no effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inheritance is a money matter. רבי יהודה lets conditions against the Torah work in money matters, so by his view the father's condition should stand.

steps.title: The source: the betrothal condition about food, clothing, and marital relations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a man betroths a woman on the condition that she has no claim to food, clothing, and marital relations. רבי מאיר says she is betrothed and the condition is cancelled. רבי יהודה says that in money matters, the condition stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If a man says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me on condition that you have no claim on me for food, clothing, and marital relations,' she is betrothed and his condition is cancelled. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: in a money matter, his condition stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows where רבי יהודה says conditions against the Torah work in money matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires a husband to give his wife food, clothing, and marital relations. רבי מאיר says no condition can cancel these. רבי יהודה says the money parts, like food and clothing, can be cancelled by a condition. This backs up the suggestion in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (introduces a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught:
One who says to a woman:
"You are hereby betrothed to me,
on condition that you have no claim on me
for food, clothing, and marital relations"
phrases.notes: These are the three things a husband owes his wife (שמות 21:10).

phrases.english: she is betrothed,
and his condition is cancelled;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
in a money matter, his condition stands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יהודה's view quoted in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה lets a condition against the Torah work in money matters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about betrothal with a condition cancelling food, clothing, and marital relations.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה agrees: the wife gave up her rights, the son did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. In the betrothal case, the wife knew about the condition and agreed to give up her rights. Here the son never agreed to give up his share, so even רבי יהודה would say the father's condition fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it is רבי יהודה: there, she knew and gave up her rights. Here, he did not give anything up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 7. The משנה can follow רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's condition works because the person losing out, the wife, heard it and agreed. In the inheritance case, the son loses out, but the father made the condition by himself and the son never agreed. So the two cases are not alike, and the משנה fits everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: A condition against the Torah in money matters works for רבי יהודה only when the person who loses out knows about it and agrees. A father cannot cancel his son's inheritance on his own.
steps.confusionAlert: The difference is not the topic (marriage versus inheritance). Both are money matters. The difference is whether the person losing out agreed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of רבי יהודה's rule. A condition can take away someone's money rights only with that person's agreement.

phrases.english: Even if you say it is Rabbi Yehuda:
there, she knew and gave up her rights;
here, he did not give anything up.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the son who loses out. His father made the condition, but the son never agreed to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 7 by showing that the case in Step 8 is different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must go against רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignored a key difference. In the betrothal case the person losing out agreed, but in the inheritance case the son never agreed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה fits even רבי יהודה, because the son never gave up his inheritance rights.

steps.title: רב יוסף: 'My firstborn' versus 'a firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a father who says 'So-and-so, my son, is my firstborn' gives him פי שנים. If he only says 'So-and-so is a firstborn,' the son does not get פי שנים, because he may have meant a mother's firstborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If a man said, 'So-and-so, my son, is my firstborn,' that son takes a double portion. If he said, 'So-and-so is a firstborn,' the son does not take a double portion, because maybe he meant his mother's firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב יוסף about which words of a father prove that a son is a בכור for inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the father's first son gets the double portion. The plain word 'firstborn' is unclear, because it could mean the mother's first child, who may not be the father's first. The words 'my firstborn' tie the son to the father, so they count.

keyTerms.meaning: a double portion of the inheritance, given to the בכור
a mother's firstborn, her first child, who may not be the father's first

steps.confusionAlert: Being the mother's first child is not enough for the double portion. The inheritance law follows the father's firstborn.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the test for the whole section that follows: any evidence must show the son is the father's firstborn, not just the mother's.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If one said: "So-and-so, my son, is my firstborn"
he takes a double portion.
If he said: "So-and-so is a firstborn"
he does not take a double portion,
perhaps he was saying he is a mother's firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: proving who is the בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'My firstborn' proves the son is the father's בכור and gives him פי שנים. 'A firstborn' does not, since it could mean the mother's firstborn.

steps.title: A witness before רבה בר בר חנה: 'His father called him a foolish firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: A man tells רבה בר בר חנה that he knows someone is a בכור. Asked how, he says the father used to call the son 'foolish firstborn.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבה בר בר חנה and said: I know that this man is a firstborn. He asked him: How do you know? He answered: Because his father used to call him 'foolish firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where a witness offers evidence that someone is a בכור. This sets up רבה בר בר חנה's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness does not say the father declared 'my firstborn.' He relies on a nickname the father used. The question is whether that nickname is strong enough under רב יוסף's test.

keyTerms.meaning: I know firmly, I hold it as established
'foolish firstborn,' a nickname for a firstborn

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה,
phrases.english: There was a certain man who came before Rabba bar bar Chana,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוּחְזְקַנִי בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא בְּכוֹר.
phrases.english: he said to him: I know about this one that he is a firstborn.
He said to him: From where do you know?
Because his father would call him "foolish firstborn."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real case that tests רב יוסף's rule.
steps.raayaObject: That the man is a בכור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The father's habit of calling him 'foolish firstborn.'

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה rejects the nickname as proof
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה answers that the son may be only the mother's firstborn, because a mother's firstborn is also called 'foolish firstborn.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he is his mother's firstborn, because every mother's firstborn is also called 'foolish firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה rejects the witness's evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nickname fits a mother's firstborn just as well as a father's firstborn. Because it does not show he is the father's first son, it cannot give him פי שנים. This matches רב יוסף's reasoning in step 10.

phrases.english: Perhaps he is a mother's firstborn,
phrases.notes: This is רבה בר בר חנה answering the witness.

phrases.english: for every mother's firstborn too
they call him "foolish firstborn."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the evidence brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The nickname 'foolish firstborn' as proof of being the father's בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The nickname is also used for a mother's firstborn, so it does not prove the son is the father's first.
steps.whatToRemember: Evidence that would also fit a mother's firstborn does not prove a son is a בכור for inheritance.

steps.title: A witness before רבי חנינא: 'His saliva heals because he is a firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: A man tells רבי חנינא that someone is a בכור. His evidence is that the father used to send people to his son שכחת, saying his son is a firstborn and his saliva heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבי חנינא and said: I know that this man is a firstborn. He asked: How do you know? He answered: When people came to his father, he would tell them, 'Go to my son שכחת, because he is a firstborn and his saliva heals.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story with a different kind of evidence that someone is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the father himself called the son a firstborn and linked it to his saliva having the power to heal. The story is told as evidence that works, and the next steps explain why.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who came before Rabbi Chanina,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוּחְזְקַנִי בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא בְּכוֹר.
phrases.english: he said to him: I know about this one that he is a firstborn.
He said to him: From where do you know?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּכִי הֲווֹ אָתוּ לְגַבֵּי אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Because when people would come to his father,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ לְגַבֵּי שִׁכְחַת בְּרִי,
phrases.english: he would say to them: Go to my son Shikhchat,
because he is a firstborn and his saliva heals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case that parallels step 11 but uses different evidence.
steps.raayaObject: That the man is a בכור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The father's statement that his son is a firstborn whose saliva heals.

steps.title: But maybe he is only the mother's firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: here too, maybe the son is only his mother's firstborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he is his mother's firstborn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second story with the same doubt that worked in the first story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 this doubt was enough to reject the nickname. The father here also just said 'firstborn,' not 'my firstborn,' so why should this evidence be any better?

phrases.english: But perhaps he is a mother's firstborn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the doubt from step 12 against the evidence in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The evidence of the father's statement in the רבי חנינא story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father only said 'firstborn,' which could mean the mother's firstborn, just like the nickname in step 12.

steps.title: Only a father's firstborn has healing saliva
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a known tradition: a father's firstborn has healing saliva, and a mother's firstborn does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition: the saliva of a father's firstborn heals, but the saliva of a mother's firstborn does not heal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and explains why the second witness's evidence works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father did not just say 'firstborn.' He said his son's saliva heals, and only a father's firstborn has that power. So his words must mean his own firstborn. That fits רב יוסף's test.

keyTerms.meaning: a father's firstborn, the one who gets the double portion

steps.whatToRemember: A father's words prove a son is a בכור only if they point to the father's firstborn: 'my firstborn,' or a sign that fits only a father's firstborn, such as healing saliva. A plain 'firstborn' or the nickname 'foolish firstborn' is not enough.

phrases.english: It is learned as a tradition:
the saliva of a father's firstborn heals,
the saliva of a mother's firstborn does not heal.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two cases by a known tradition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father's mention of 'firstborn' might mean only the mother's firstborn, like the nickname in the first story.
steps.terutzMaskana: Healing saliva belongs only to a father's firstborn, so the father's words show the son is his own בכור.

steps.title: A טומטום later found male does not get the double portion
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that a טומטום who is opened and found to be male does not receive a בכור's double portion. The פסוק 'וְהָיָה הַבֵּן הַבְּכוֹר' teaches that he must be known as a son from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי says: a טומטום (a baby whose gender could not be seen) who was cut open and turned out to be a boy does not take a double portion. This is because the פסוק says 'וְהָיָה הַבֵּן הַבְּכוֹר', meaning he must be a son from the moment he came into being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אמי: a טומטום who is later found to be male cannot collect a בכור's double share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְהָיָה' (and he was) is read as connected to 'הֲוָיָה' (coming into being). A בכור gets the double portion only if he was recognized as a son from birth. A טומטום was not recognized as male when he was born, so he loses this right even though he really is male.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose gender cannot be seen because the private area is covered by skin
Was torn open, meaning the covering skin was opened
A double portion, the inheritance share of a בכור
As the פסוק says. It introduces the source in the Torah
From the moment of coming into being, meaning from birth

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say this person is not male. He really is a male son. The only issue is that he was not known to be a son at birth, so he does not get the special double portion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of being a son 'from birth', and the next step applies the same idea to בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami says:
A tumtum who was torn open and was found to be male,
does not take a double portion;
as the verse says:
"And if the firstborn son was of the hated wife"
meaning: only once he is a son from the moment he came into being.
phrases.notes: The word וְהָיָה sounds like הֲוָיָה, coming into being, so he must be known as a boy from birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories about proving who is a בכור to a new rule about who can qualify as a בכור at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום found to be male does not receive the בכור's double portion, because a בכור must be a recognized son from birth.

steps.title: The same rule applies to בן סורר ומורה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that a טומטום later found male also cannot be judged as a בן סורר ומורה, based on the word 'יִהְיֶה' in that פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק says: such a person is also not judged as a בן סורר ומורה, because the פסוק says 'כִּי יִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה', meaning he must be a son from the moment he came into being.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק takes רבי אמי's rule and applies it to another law. A טומטום found to be male cannot become a בן סורר ומורה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about בן סורר ומורה also uses a form of the word 'to be' (יִהְיֶה). It is read the same way as by בכור: it means a son from birth. The word 'אַף' (also) shows this is an addition to רבי אמי's ruling, not a disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: Also. It adds a second law to the first
The stubborn and rebellious son described in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: A טומטום who is later found to be male really is a son. But two laws that the Torah introduces with the word 'to be' (הָיָה / יִהְיֶה), בכור and בן סורר ומורה, require him to have been a known son from birth. So he is excluded from both.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵינוֹ נִידּוֹן כְּבֵן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה,
phrases.english: He is also not judged as a stubborn and rebellious son,
as the verse says:
"If there will be to a man a stubborn and rebellious son"
meaning: only once he is a son from the moment he came into being.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף אֵינוֹ נִידּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אמי's 'son from birth' reading from בכור to בן סורר ומורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום found to be male is not judged as a בן סורר ומורה, since that also requires being a son from birth.
